The image shows a corn leaf with distinctive symptoms:

- **Broad, pale yellow-to-white streaking** running parallel to the leaf veins, spanning much of the leaf width
- The streaking is elongated and follows the leaf's vascular pattern
- Green tissue interspersed between pale/yellow stripes
- No pustules, no necrotic lesions, no spots — purely chlorotic/mosaic streaking

This pattern of pale yellow streaking parallel to veins is characteristic of **Maize Streak Virus**, which causes bright yellow-white streaking along the full length of leaves, following the veins. This distinguishes it from Maize Dwarf Mosaic Virus (which causes more mosaic mottling) and Corn Stunt (which causes yellowing with reddening). The broad, continuous, vein-parallel light stripes are the hallmark of Maize Streak Virus.
